raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Adds test_mtp_acceptance_length() to cover the regression class demonstrated by vllm#33771 (MTP acceptance fix revert). The test runs 80 MT-Bench prompts at temp=0 on deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3 with 4-way TP and FP8 quantization, asserting mean acceptance length (1 + accepted/drafts) stays within rtol of a pinned baseline. Also adds the corresponding nightly CI step on 4xB200 in spec_decode.yaml.

Also fixes a pre-existing bug in get_mt_bench_prompts() where enable_multimodal_chat was missing from the SimpleNamespace, causing runtime failures with current datasets.

**Need buildkite to run for final confirmation**, which needs hardware upgrades

## Code Review

This pull request introduces regression tests for Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) acceptance length, specifically targeting DeepSeek-V3 on B200 GPUs. The changes include a new Buildkite step and a dedicated test suite in `test_acceptance_length.py`. Feedback focuses on critical configuration issues: the `expected_acceptance_length` is currently a placeholder and must be calibrated for the test to be effective, and the `gpu_memory_utilization` is set too low (0.7) to accommodate the DeepSeek-V3 FP8 weights on the specified hardware, which will cause initialization failures.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `expected_acceptance_length` is currently set to a placeholder value (`1.60`). For a regression test to be effective in CI, it must be calibrated with a verified baseline. Please update this value to the actual measured mean acceptance length for DeepSeek-V3 MTP on the MT-Bench dataset before merging.

nodes.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `gpu_memory_utilization` of `0.7` is too low for DeepSeek-V3 (671B parameters). In FP8, the model weights alone require approximately 671 GB. On 4x 189 GB GPUs (total 756 GB), the weights occupy ~88.7% of the total VRAM. Setting utilization to `0.7` will cause vLLM to fail during initialization because the weights exceed the reserved memory (which would be ~529 GB). This should be increased to at least `0.9` to accommodate the weights and the MLA KV cache.

```suggestion
            gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
```

I really don't see why we need a new test implementation here, instead of adding some parameters to one of our existing tests.
2. Can we also add DSV4-Flash NVFP4? So we can cover both new and old arch.
3. We should also cover GSM8k correctness, as we do in the other tests.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `gpu_memory_utilization` of `0.7` is too low for DeepSeek-V3 (671B parameters). In FP8, the model weights alone require approximately 671 GB. On 4x 189 GB GPUs (total 756 GB), the weights occupy ~88.7% of the total VRAM. Setting utilization to `0.7` will cause vLLM to fail during initialization because the weights exceed the reserved memory (which would be ~529 GB). This should be increased to at least `0.9` to accommodate the weights and the MLA KV cache.

```suggestion
            gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
```

## Code Review

This pull request introduces regression tests for Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) acceptance length, specifically targeting DeepSeek-V3 on B200 GPUs. The changes include a new Buildkite step and a dedicated test suite in `test_acceptance_length.py`. Feedback focuses on critical configuration issues: the `expected_acceptance_length` is currently a placeholder and must be calibrated for the test to be effective, and the `gpu_memory_utilization` is set too low (0.7) to accommodate the DeepSeek-V3 FP8 weights on the specified hardware, which will cause initialization failures.

1. Can we check what the difference is between the test_acceptance_length tests and the spec decode E2E and dedicated MTP tests? I feel like we need some consolidation here. I really don't see why we need a new test implementation here, instead of adding some parameters to one of our existing tests.
2. Can we also add DSV4-Flash NVFP4? So we can cover both new and old arch.
